newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil fears giant rescue bid to free drug suspect.
newsitem.headline: Brazil fears giant rescue bid to free drug suspect.

text.p: Brazilian authorities fear the Medellin drug cartel may launch a "giant operation" to rescue a Colombian woman who is in jail in Rio while awaiting extradition to the United States, according to court documents.

Mary Valencia, 43, who was arrested in February, is an important Colombian crime figure and there are signs cartel members "are planning a giant operation to rescue her, including on Brazilian territory," the documents said without elaborating.

Valencia was questioned on Monday by Judge Ilmar Galvao of Brazil's highest court at a Rio police station rather than in the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) "for security reasons," a court spokesman said.
Valencia is accused of selling 1,595 pounds (725 kg) of cocaine in California over a 17-year period and U.S. authorities have requested her extradition, the documents said.
The full 11-member STF is expected to rule on the extradition request, but no date has been set.
